statecraft.title: Sub-districts of Mandatory Palestine in force on 15 May 1948 (true lines, not hex-snapped)
statecraft.review: Sensitivity review by the controller on the owner's behalf (owner-delegated, 2026-10-11): accepted, with the Mandate frontier outlined and the near-frontier shore hexes (Taba; the shore hex west of Rafah's frontier; the Lisan) as baked. Display rule (controller ruling, owner-delegated, 2026-10-11): the hex that holds a Gazette-listed place always takes that place's sub-district, never outside (tools/borders_bake.py rule 5; it puts Rafah town's hex (-15, 31) in Gaza and Metulla's hex (15, 1) in Safad, which the centre rule had left outside). These true lines are not changed by it.
statecraft.provenance: Hebrew name_he follows the Palestine Gazette headings in research_notes/Map borders/subdistrict-names-and-amendments-1947-48.md section 2; the 1 January 1947 to 28 April 1948 amendment check is closed (owner ruling, 23 October 2026, #196 comment 6359825082). Remaining gaps from the note's section 3.3: 29 April to 14 May 1948 was not checked; the 1948 index is a typescript of unknown origin and was only partly read; the 1947 Hebrew schedule was not found; the Schedule's village lists were not re-checked.

statecraft.licence_note: Government of Palestine works of 1945-47. Copyright: the Copyright Act 1911, extended to Palestine in 1924, gave government works 50 years from publication, so these ran out by the end of 1997 in Palestine's successor law (Israel kept the 1911 Act until its 2007 Copyright Act took effect in 2008) and in the UK (Crown copyright, CDPA 1988 s.163 and its transition). Commons tags scan (a) {{PD-UK-Gov}} and scan (b) {{PD-UKGov}}{{PD-IsraelGov}}. Caveat: like the 1948-60 Government Press Office photos (docs/oss/DECISIONS.md D-P) they were still protected on 1 January 1996, so the URAA may have restored a US copyright in the map's drawing until about 2041-42 (95 years from 1946-47). What this file takes is factual: where legally defined administrative lines run (the Proclamation is a legislative text), redrawn by our own method; no image is copied, and US copyright does not protect facts (Feist), so a possible URAA copyright in the drawing does not reach this data. Decision D-B (owner-delegated, 2026-10-11): allowed; facts redrawn, no image copied. This file, like content/, is CC BY-SA 4.0; its coast follows the Copernicus DEM (NOTICE).

sources.cite: The Palestine Gazette No. 1552, Supplement No. 2, 30 January 1947, pp. 125-133: Administrative Divisions (Amendment) Proclamation, 1947 (in force 1 January 1947). Revokes and replaces the whole Schedule of the Administrative Divisions Proclamation, 1939: the six districts and sixteen sub-districts by their villages.

statecraft.method: tools/borders_digitise.py docstring: red overprint + boundary dots, closed, flood-labelled from each sub-district's chief town, medial line, coverage-simplified at about 120 m.
statecraft.accuracy: about +-1 km. Source map 1:750,000 (a 0.3 mm line is 225 m); georeference rms 0.17 km; areas -4.1% to +3.7% against Village Statistics 1945; a second print digitised alike agrees to a mean 0.11-0.23 km, at most 1.23 km. Caveats: the Village Statistics areas follow the 1945 Schedule (Gazette No. 1415), not the 1947 one, so 1947 adjustments count as error; Beersheba's figure (12,577,000 dunams) is a rounded estimate, so its check is nominal; Gaza low and Beersheba high point at the Gaza/Beersheba line (the Bureir connector). Uncertain segments (under labels, connectors, the Metulla tip) to about +-1.5 km.
statecraft.coast: Seaward edges follow the game's Copernicus DEM coastline (sea at 0 m) and the Dead Sea at its 1948 level (-392 m): coast, not a boundary. Lake Tiberias is inside the Tiberias sub-district.

uncertain_segments.why: Ras en Naqura: the Lebanese frontier extended a few pixels to the DEM sea
Rosh Pinna: the Syrian frontier runs under the 'Rosh Pinna' label
Afula: the Galilee/Samaria district boundary runs under the 'Afula' label
Bureir: the Gaza/Beersheba sub-district boundary runs under the 'Bureir' label
Gulf of Aqaba: the Transjordan frontier extended a few pixels to the DEM sea
Jaffa/Ramle boundary: its coastal end extended a few pixels to the DEM sea

Metulla: listed under safad in the 1947 Schedule (p. 127 (Safad Sub-District: 'Metulla (includes Deir Mamas, Hura and Kafr Kila)')) but drawn on the frontier's tip at 1:750,000; land within 0.8 km kept in safad (coordinates: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metula)
narrow salients of solid lines (the frontier): the coarse closing fills them; a fine closing (6 px) gives each back to the region on its side where that side is unambiguous
